audit.whatIsWrong: win[0..2] read Sett while the matchup's own early text says 'levels 1-3 are yours to bully' and whys[0] says you beat him at level 1.
audit.why: The two layers agree with each other, and I have no independent basis to overrule the chart, so I left it and flagged the contradiction instead of inventing a power shift.
audit.corrected: Chart untouched. See questionsForUser — the packet's levelChart for this pairing reads Pantheon/Pantheon/Skill/Sett/Sett/Sett/Skill, which is a third answer again.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes named no abilities and carried no numbers.
audit.why: Haymaker is 18/16.5/15/13.5/12s, Facebreaker 16s at 490, The Show Stopper 120s at rank 1. Those are the actual spike gates.
audit.corrected: Haymaker's 18s and The Show Stopper's 120s written into the level-6 spike, breakdown.cooldowns and report[5]; Knuckle Down's max-health scaling added to the first-item spike.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two mechanical errors. (a) 'Bait his E grab: if he whiffs the slow projectile, he has no way to catch you' — Facebreaker is not a projectile and it is not dodged like one. (b) 'his R suppresses you' — The Show Stopper is a carry-and-slam, not a suppression.
audit.why: Riot: Facebreaker 'pulls in all enemies on opposite sides of him, dealing damage and stunning them. If enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead of stunned' — so in a 1v1 with no minions flanking him it slows you and does not stun at all, which is the opposite of what the page implies. The Show Stopper 'carries an enemy champion through the air and slams them into the ground'.
audit.corrected: Facebreaker described as a 490-range pull that only stuns when enemies are on both sides — 1v1 it slows. The Show Stopper described as a carry-and-slam.

audit.whatIsWrong: The matchup never says that your own poke charges Haymaker, and never says which way Aegis Assault faces.
audit.why: Riot: 'Sett passively stores damage he takes as Grit. On cast, Sett expends all stored Grit to gain a shield and punch an area, dealing true damage in the center.' Every Comet Spear you land is ammunition for that punch. And Aegis Assault is invulnerable from the front only.
audit.corrected: Written into early, whys[2] and wants.foe[0]: poke feeds Grit, so trade to kill rather than to chip; and face the shield at the punch.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing said The Show Stopper ends an Aegis Assault channel.
audit.why: Aegis Assault is a channel; The Show Stopper physically carries you out of it. This is the level-6 flip the page gestured at without naming.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Passive shield + Q poke wins level 1 outright' in phases[0].why and breakdown.early.
audit.why: Pantheon has no passive shield — Mortal Will empowers his next spell. Sett's genuine level-1 tools are Pit Grit's missing-health regen and Knuckle Down's max-health hits.
audit.corrected: Both rewritten around the real abilities.

edits.before: Sett is a juggernaut with no early dash and zero ranged poke, so levels 1-3 are yours to bully. At level 1 your point-and-click W stun plus a Q tap out-trades him before his W has any stored damage to fire back. Poke the held, long-range Q from max distance so he eats it walking up to farm, and at 2-3 commit the W-stun in, empowered-Q, then hold E to face his return double-punch — his block damage goes to zero through your shield channel. Bait his E grab: if he whiffs the slow projectile, he has no way to catch you.
edits.after: Sett is a juggernaut with no dash and zero ranged poke, so levels 1-3 are yours to bully. At level 1 your point-and-click Shield Vault plus a Comet Spear tap out-trades him before Haymaker has stored any Grit to fire back. Poke the thrown Comet Spear from max distance as he walks up to farm — but every point of damage he takes is Grit banked into that punch. At 2-3 commit the W-stun, empowered-Q, then face Aegis Assault at his return punch; it only blocks the front. Facebreaker pulls at 490 and only stuns when enemies are on both sides of him — 1v1 it just slows you.

edits.before: From level 4-5 your kill pressure dips as he stacks HP and his W starts storing real damage off the trades you give him. Once he hits 6, the lane flips: his R suppresses you out of your E channel and a full-charge W smash does true damage your shields don't reduce on your squishy frame. Stop face-checking all-ins here — instead, use your level advantage on the map. Grand Starfall a sidelane or river gank while he's stuck farming, because your 1v1 edge over him is shrinking every level.
edits.after: From level 4-5 your kill pressure dips as he stacks HP and Haymaker banks real damage off the trades you give him. Once he hits 6 the lane flips: The Show Stopper carries you through the air and slams you, which ends an Aegis Assault channel outright, and a full-Grit Haymaker deals true damage in its centre that armour does not reduce. Stop face-checking all-ins here — use your level advantage on the map instead. Grand Starfall a sidelane or river gank while he is stuck farming, because your 1v1 edge shrinks every level.

edits.before: By two items Sett out-scales you cleanly — his grit passive turns his missing HP into a true-damage W, and Steraks plus Bork make him a wall your plateaued burst can't break. You do not win the extended duel anymore; his R can flip you in any skirmish. Your whole game had to be the lead you built before level 6 and the roams you cashed it into. Play for picks with R and let your team handle the front-to-back; never solo-commit into a grit-fed Sett late.
edits.after: By two items Sett out-scales you cleanly — Pit Grit turns his missing health into regen, Knuckle Down's next two hits scale off your max health, and Steraks plus Bork make him a wall your plateaued burst cannot break. Play for picks with R and never solo-commit into a Grit-fed Sett late.

notes: Two claims in this matchup were mechanically wrong in ways that change how the lane is played. First, 'Bait his E grab: if he whiffs the slow projectile, he has no way to catch you' — Facebreaker is a 490-range pull, not a projectile, and Riot's text is explicit that it only stuns when enemies are on opposite sides of him; in an isolated 1v1 it slows you instead. A player waiting to sidestep a missile is waiting for something that does not exist. Second, 'his R suppresses you out of your E channel' — The Show Stopper carries and slams, it is not a suppression. The page also never mentioned the single most important thing about laning into Sett: Haymaker banks the damage you deal him as Grit, so max-range Comet Spear chip is literally loading his punch. That is now stated in early, whys[2] and wants.foe[0]. Flagged, not changed.
